spans.claim: The victim was shot in bed with a .38 caliber bullet
spans.anchor: Death was caused by an intrathoracic hemorrhage, due to a bullet shot into the left chest
spans.span: Death was caused by an intrathoracic hemorrhage, due to a bullet shot into the left chest.

spans.claim: No footprints were found outside the house after the murder
spans.anchor: Nowhere near a window, nowhere near a door, was there a footprint nor a break in the snow
spans.span: Nowhere near a window, nowhere near a door, was there a footprint nor a break in the snow of any kind.

spans.claim: Family members were locked in their rooms with keys collected
spans.anchor: Irene found seven keys in my brother’s room, and used one key to unlock each door

spans.claim: Neal Quilter was locked in his room at the time of the murder
spans.anchor: Lucy came running into my room in her nightgown, screaming my name
spans.span: At about the second bang, Lucy came running into my room in her nightgown, screaming my name, and what was it, and that her door was locked.

spans.claim: The rope hanging from the window was covered with snow and unused
spans.anchor: The rope was covered with snow, and there was not a handprint in the snow on the window sill
spans.span: But the rope was covered with snow, and there was not a handprint in the snow on the window sill, nor a footprint in the new snow on the roof.

spans.claim: Olympe’s revolver was a .32 Colt’s and was unloaded
spans.anchor: It was Uncle Phineas’s old .32 Colt’s. I broke it. The chambers were all empty
spans.span: It was Uncle Phineas's old .32 Colt's. I broke it. The chambers were all empty; so it could not have been either harmful or useful.

spans.claim: The murder weapon was a .38 caliber Colt’s
spans.anchor: The bullet, which Dr. Joe had removed from Father’s body, had been fired from a .38 Colt’s of fairly recent make
spans.span: I told her then what I should have told her in the beginning, and what she had had no opportunity to know without being told, since she was not at the inquest: That the bullet, which Dr. Joe had removed from Father's body, had been fired from a .38 Colt's of fairly recent make.

spans.claim: Dr. Joseph Elm confessed to assisting in the murder
spans.anchor: I killed Dick. That’s a damn lie! And you know it! Take it easy, boy, if you can. I’m sorry

spans.claim: The victim was terminally ill with cancer
spans.anchor: Your father’s ailment was cancer. He knew it, and I knew it
spans.span: You see, my boy, your father's ailment was cancer. He knew it, and I knew it.

spans.claim: The victim planned his own death to look like murder
spans.anchor: Dick planned alone, and we planned together. By Gad, Neal, but we tried
spans.span: Well, Dick planned alone, and we planned together. By Gad, Neal, but we tried.

spans.claim: The victim’s last words mentioned a red mask
spans.anchor: He said, quite distinctly, “Red mask.” There was no shaking her certainty about that

spans.claim: The red mask was found in Olympe’s room
spans.anchor: Lying on the floor, directly beneath the open cupola window, was a mask, large enough to cover a man’s entire face, cut roughly out of bright red satin
spans.span: Lying on the floor, directly beneath the open cupola window, was a mask, large enough to cover a man's entire face, cut roughly out of bright red satin.

spans.claim: Neal Quilter suffered amnesia about the murder
spans.anchor: I am swearing to you that, for the past two years or more, until about half an hour ago, I have thought exactly the same thing about myself

spans.claim: Neal Quilter’s letters contain clues to the truth
spans.anchor: Lucy’s second letter to you makes the first track. Maybe it would take a crime analyst to discover it
spans.span: Lucy's second letter to you makes the first track. Maybe it would take a crime analyst to discover it; but, in the third letter, the path starts off, good and deep, and follows straight along through Neal's last letter to you-not a misstep, not a detour, not a doubt.

spans.claim: The family’s insurance policy had lapsed but was paid by Dr. Elm
spans.anchor: I made that last payment, he said, and sat down

spans.claim: The family dog Whatof was chained at the front door
spans.anchor: We have kept Whatof chained by the front door and Keeper chained by the back door
spans.span: We have kept Whatof chained by the front door and Keeper chained by the back door.

spans.claim: The inquest jury returned a verdict of death by person unknown
spans.anchor: Died on the night of October eighth, from the results of a gunshot wound inflicted by person or persons unknown
spans.span: Two hours and ten minutes, Jude, while we hung around waiting, before they brought in their verdict: Died on the night of October eighth, from the results of a gunshot wound inflicted by person or persons unknown.

spans.claim: The victim’s bed was moved slightly
spans.anchor: The bed had been moved three or four inches at the foot—pulled along over the carpet
spans.span: The bed had been moved three or four inches at the foot-pulled along over the carpet, I mean, as if some fairly hefty weight had been tugging on it.

spans.claim: Irene Quilter was locked out of her room and slept on the sofa
spans.anchor: She found that the door was locked. She turned around and sneaked straight downstairs again, and fixed herself a bed, with Indian blankets, on the sofa

spans.claim: The victim’s window was open with a rope tied to the bed
spans.anchor: The window was wide open from the bottom. There was a thick rope hanging over the sill and out of it
spans.span: The window was wide open from the bottom. There was a thick rope hanging over the sill and out of it.
